details.description: DeepSeek-V3.2 is DeepSeek's mixture-of-experts chat and reasoning model, with 685 billion parameters per its Hugging Face model card, released December 1, 2025 as the official successor to the experimental DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp. It uses DeepSeek Sparse Attention for cheaper long-context inference and, per DeepSeek's launch announcement, is the first DeepSeek model to combine a 'thinking' mode -- extended reasoning before acting -- with tool use, alongside a faster non-thinking mode. DeepSeek briefly served it as the standard deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner model, but DeepSeek's changelog shows those two names were repointed to the newer DeepSeek-V4-Flash in April 2026 and slated for discontinuation by July 2026, and V4-Flash was itself later retired in favor of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Amazon Bedrock still lists deepseek.v3.2 with an 'Active' lifecycle, a 164K-token context window, and an 8K-token output limit.
advantages: Scores 82.4 on GPQA Diamond, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 85 on MMLU-Pro, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 70 on SWE-bench Verified, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Combines a thinking mode for extended reasoning with tool calls and a faster non-thinking mode, per DeepSeek's V3.2 launch announcement.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's changelog shows the deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner names that served V3.2 were repointed to newer V4 models starting April 2026, with the intervening V4-Flash name itself later retired in favor of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
Text only; no image or audio input or output.
use_cases: General-purpose chat with a switchable thinking/non-thinking reasoning mode.
Agentic workflows that interleave long-chain reasoning with tool calls.
Long-context document analysis up to a 164,000-token context window.

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens values (163840 and 164000) both match AWS Bedrock's stated 164K context window (the two figures look like rounding differences between Bud's providers). One of catalog's two max_output_tokens values (8000) matches Bedrock's stated 8K output limit, but the second (163840) could not be corroborated: DeepSeek's own current docs no longer document the retired V3.2 model directly, only V4-Pro/V4.1-Flash, so this could not be checked against a maker source. Total parameter count (685B) is DeepSeek's own Hugging Face figure; active-parameter count and exact knowledge cutoff for the chat/thinking modes were not stated on the pages read. A GitHub repo exists for the related DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp release but was not opened, and none was confirmed for V3.2 itself, so github_url is left null. Corrected: the pricing page itself never names 'v3.2', 'deepseek-chat' or 'deepseek-reasoner' as retired -- it only lists 'deepseek-v4-flash' and 'deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp' as retired legacy names now served by V4.1-Flash. The changelog page (already in sources) is the actual support for V3.2's aliases being superseded: deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner were repointed to V4-Flash in April 2026 and slated for discontinuation by 2026-07-24, and V4-Flash was itself later retired in favor of V4.1-Flash.
